clue.text: Its market value may, presumably, be assessed on gross weight

definitions.text: Its market value may, presumably, be assessed on gross weight

parts.words: Its market value may, presumably, be assessed on gross weight
parts.note: gross weight reads as heavy bulk rather than total weight: cattle bred for slaughter are sold by how much meat they carry

explanation.surface: A remark about pricing goods by their total weight including packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross weight' sounds like a trade term for total weight; here it means the beast is fat, and fat beasts fetch more.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock fattened for the butcher is sold on how heavy it has grown.

clue.text: He can't claim copyright

parts.note: copyright read as 'copy right': this man copies documents or signatures exactly, but cannot own them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copyright' splits into 'copy right', which is exactly what a faker of banknotes does.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter copies accurately but holds no legal right to the work.

clue.text: Gear needed to foil the fugitive ?

definitions.meaning: bringing down a runner, as in rugby or football, stops his escape

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the move that brings a running player or fleeing thief to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing equipment shares its name with the act of bringing down a runner.

clue.text: I get involved with a rum lot causing commotion

indicators.note: to get involved is to become tangled, so the letters are mixed up together

explanation.surface: Joining a disreputable crowd brings trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved with' mixes I with RUM LOT; 'a' and 'causing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of great disturbance or upheaval.

clue.text: They have their crosses, politically speaking

definitions.text: They have their crosses, politically speaking

parts.words: They have their crosses, politically speaking
parts.note: crosses are not burdens but the marks voters put on ballot papers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' suggests troubles to bear; in politics it is the X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters in an electoral district each mark a ballot with an X.

clue.text: Crafty blows

definitions.meaning: read as 'craft-y', plural of small boats: sailing fishing boats
slaps or smart hits with the open hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like an adjective meaning cunning; it is a playful plural of craft, small fishing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sailing fishing vessels share their name with sharp slaps.

clue.text: In the character of Othello ?

parts.note: character means style rather than personality: Othello was a Moor of Venice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' invites jealousy or nobility; it means the style of the Moors, as in architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is 'the Moor of Venice', so his style is that of the North African people.

clue.text: Order for a grey coat, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone placing an order for a grey overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GREY COAT; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A class or division, as in an order of things.

clue.text: The main colour

parts.note: 'the main' is a poetic name for the ocean, so this is the ocean's colour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal'; in verse 'the main' means the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluish-green shade of ocean water.

clue.text: Maria Edgeworth's castle

parts.note: the title of Maria Edgeworth's 1800 novel names a castle after an exorbitant kind of rent

explanation.walkthrough: Maria Edgeworth was an Anglo-Irish novelist whose best-known book is 'Castle' followed by a term for extortionate rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Her novel's title castle is named for an extortionate rent charged by landlords.

clue.text: A pair to make up for a role in Shakespeare

indicators.note: to make up is to assemble or compose, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Two actors put together to fill a part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' rearranges PAIR TO; the opening 'A' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Merchant of Venice who disguises herself as a lawyer.

clue.text: There are at least two ways of getting to this point

definitions.text: There are at least two ways of getting to this point

parts.words: There are at least two ways of getting to this point
parts.note: ways are roads, and the point is the place where two of them meet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ways' sounds like methods; they are literal roads meeting at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two roads meet in town is the corner of a block.

clue.text: Slippery customer wearing a bib looks fishy

indicators.note: the eel has the second piece on, so it is joined straight onto it

parts.note: an eel is the classic slippery customer
the bib is a small fish of the cod family, also called the pout

explanation.surface: Someone shifty in a bib seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bib' is not a baby's napkin but the fish also called pout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something with the look of a fish, as this eel-like sea creature has.

clue.text: It's responsible for many an outbreak of fire

definitions.text: It's responsible for many an outbreak of fire

parts.words: It's responsible for many an outbreak of fire
parts.note: fire here means the shooting of a gun, not flames: the small lever that sets off each shot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak of fire' suggests an arsonist or a spark; it is a gun going off.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever squeezed to discharge a gun causes each shot.

clue.text: The one to put one's shirt on

definitions.text: The one to put one's shirt on

parts.note: putting one's shirt on means betting everything on a horse, but also hanging a shirt on a drying frame

explanation.walkthrough: To 'put one's shirt on' a horse is British slang for staking everything on it; the answer is a frame for airing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame where laundered garments are hung to dry is literally where shirts go.

clue.text: A call to be doubly armed ?

definitions.text: A call to be doubly armed

parts.words: A call to be doubly armed
parts.note: a call is a bid in bridge, and a club is both a suit and a weapon, so the bid names a pair of cudgels

explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge a 'call' is a bid; this bid names a suit that is also a weapon, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge bid of a pair in the black suit sounds like two cudgels.

clue.text: Stop! It's the whole range of notes

definitions.meaning: an organ stop, in particular one of the main foundation stops
the full compass of a voice or instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop!' looks like a command; it is an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a principal organ stop and the entire compass of musical pitch.

clue.text: Surely not part of a brave's head-dress?

definitions.text: Surely not part of a brave's head-dress?

parts.words: Surely not part of a brave's head-dress?
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior who wears plumes, but this plume is the symbol of cowardice

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a white plume was handed to men thought cowardly, so no brave would wear one.
explanation.definitionFit: This plume is the traditional emblem of cowardice, the opposite of bravery.

clue.text: Blow up into a general disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An explosion causing a widespread upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges GENERAL; 'into a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a photograph or image larger is to magnify it.

clue.text: Suitable material for a stretcher

parts.note: a stretcher is not a carrying frame but anything that stretches: this material stretches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests carrying the injured; read it as something that stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbery material that springs back is made for stretching.

clue.text: Cleric who is of a forgiving nature?

definitions.meaning: Pope wrote 'to err is human, to forgive' is godly

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense draws on Pope's line that forgiving is godlike.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is called by the same word as something godlike, which Pope said forgiveness is.

clue.text: Scores just miss striking gold

parts.note: in archery the gold is the bullseye; the ring next to it gives these near-miss scores

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking gold' suggests a lucky find; in archery and shooting the gold is the centre of the target.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots landing in the ring just outside the bullseye score these.

clue.text: For that matter, wherefore was Juliet one ?

definitions.text: For that matter, wherefore was Juliet one

parts.words: For that matter, wherefore was Juliet one
parts.note: echoes Juliet's 'wherefore art thou Romeo', turning the question onto her own family name

explanation.walkthrough: Juliet asks why Romeo must be a Montague; the clue asks why she belonged to the rival house.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family in Shakespeare's Verona was the house feuding with the Montagues.

clue.text: This reception at an inn would be a novelty

definitions.text: This reception at an inn would be a novelty

parts.words: This reception at an inn would be a novelty
parts.note: read 'at an inn' as 'with an N placed at the front': this applause then becomes a word for renewal or newness

explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds the answer backwards: put N before the enthusiastic reception and you get NOVATION, a making-new.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing round of applause is a warm reception for a performer.

clue.text: Not like that certain party?

parts.note: 'that certain party' is someone who is certain; to be unlike them is to be in doubt

explanation.walkthrough: 'That certain party' normally means an unnamed person; here 'certain' is taken literally as confident.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking confidence is the opposite of being certain.

clue.text: A betting reform, however small, can be irritating

definitions.text: A betting reform, however small, can be irritating

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A change to gambling rules, even a minor one, annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges A BETTING; the whole clue then describes the result, a tiny wound that itches.
explanation.definitionFit: The bite of a tiny insect is small yet itchy and annoying.

clue.text: Divides the sky with the moon, said Byron

definitions.text: Divides the sky with the moon, said Byron

parts.words: Divides the sky with the moon, said Byron
parts.note: quotes Childe Harold: 'The moon is up, and yet it is not night; ... divides the sky with her'

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's lines describe the evening sky shared by the rising moon and the setting day.
explanation.definitionFit: At dusk the departing day's glow shares the sky with the rising moon.

clue.text: Jumpers for outdoor games ?

parts.note: jumpers are sweaters worn for sport, but also leaping insects, which share their name with the bat-and-ball game

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a sweater; the clue suggests cricket sweaters but means chirping, leaping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaping, chirping insects share their name with the summer bat-and-ball game.
